meta.name: Beacon seed research graph
meta.disclaimer: Prototype research-navigation data. Scores are transparent heuristics, not clinical probabilities or medical advice.

query.label: SCN2A-related disorder
query.summary: A neurodevelopmental disorder spectrum associated with pathogenic SCN2A variants. Functional effect matters: gain-, loss-, and mixed-function variants can map to different phenotype patterns.

score_model.label: Research Match Score
score_model.note: Prototype ranking heuristic for research navigation. It is not a validated clinical similarity metric.

matches.label: SCN8A-related disorder
matches.why: Gain-of-function SCN2A and SCN8A variants can both increase sodium-channel activity and are associated with early developmental epilepsies. Their clinical expression is not identical, so the match is for research collaboration rather than treatment transfer.

asset.name: International SCN8A Patient Registry
asset.description: A caregiver-reported longitudinal registry built to improve understanding of the SCN8A disease spectrum and natural history.

reuse.reason: A reusable template for longitudinal rare-disease data collection.
Seizure and developmental trajectories are relevant across related developmental epilepsies.
Both disorders benefit from linking variant information to phenotype.
Potentially comparable, but exact outcome definitions require expert harmonization.
Channel- and disease-specific biology may not transfer.
A research match does not establish treatment equivalence or clinical guidance.

milestone.title: Cross-disease natural-history harmonization
milestone.goal: Create a shared core of natural-history measures that can support future trial readiness while preserving disease-specific fields.
milestone.why_now: Both communities study sodium-channel neurodevelopmental disease, and SCN8A already has mature longitudinal registry infrastructure.
steps: Compare SCN2A DRAGONFLY and SCN8A registry schemas.
Identify common seizure, developmental, and genotype/phenotype fields.
Have domain experts mark fields as shared, adaptable, or disease-specific.
Pilot a harmonized core dataset for cross-disease natural-history analysis.
needs_validation: Whether the relevant SCN2A functional subgroup is biologically comparable to the selected SCN8A subgroup.
Whether endpoint definitions and age windows are sufficiently compatible.
Whether patient organizations and investigators agree on data governance and consent.

matches.label: SCN3A-related neurodevelopmental disorder
matches.why: Published functional work shows gain-of-function SCN3A variants in early infantile epileptic encephalopathy, and cross-channel studies group gain-of-function SCN2A/SCN3A/SCN8A variants around related early-onset epilepsy biology.

asset.name: Published SCN3A electrophysiology assay designs
asset.description: Patch-clamp approaches used to characterize gain-of-function SCN3A variants can inform how related sodium-channel mechanisms are compared.

reuse.reason: The assay concept directly measures sodium-channel functional effects.
Gain/loss/mixed-function characterization is central to both disorders.
Protocol structure is reusable, but channel expression and construct details differ.
SCN3A cohorts are smaller and clinical phenotypes are not interchangeable.
Functional similarity does not justify cross-disease treatment recommendations.

milestone.title: Cross-channel functional assay benchmark
milestone.goal: Create a standardized comparison of functional-effect measurements across SCN2A and SCN3A variants.
milestone.why_now: The mechanistic overlap is strong, while research infrastructure is thinner than SCN8A, making assay reuse a more defensible first collaboration.
steps: Map assay variables used in SCN2A and SCN3A functional studies.
Define a shared minimum set of electrophysiology measurements.
Select representative gain-of-function variants from both genes.
Use the shared panel to test whether mechanistic similarity holds across variants.
needs_validation: Whether the same cellular model is appropriate for both channels.
Whether functional similarity predicts clinically useful shared endpoints.

matches.label: SCN1A-related Dravet syndrome
matches.why: SCN1A disorders share sodium-channel and epilepsy phenotypes, but classic Dravet syndrome is usually mechanistically different from the SCN2A gain-of-function branch. The prototype therefore ranks it below SCN8A and SCN3A despite strong phenotype overlap.

asset.name: Mature Dravet natural-history and outcome-measure ecosystem
asset.description: A mature disease area can provide examples of seizure and developmental outcome measurement, but mechanism-specific conclusions should remain separate.

reuse.reason: Outcome-measure design can be informative across epilepsy studies.
Patient-centered measurement frameworks can inform other rare epilepsies.
Study architecture may be adaptable while disease-specific variables remain separate.
Classic Dravet biology differs materially from SCN2A gain-of-function disease.
Mechanistic differences make direct treatment transfer unsafe and scientifically unsupported.

milestone.title: Outcome-measure benchmarking
milestone.goal: Use mature Dravet study design as a reference for measurement quality, not as a biological or therapeutic proxy.
milestone.why_now: The phenotype overlap makes outcome design informative, while the mechanism mismatch is an important guardrail the atlas should expose.
steps: Identify generalizable seizure and caregiver-reported outcome concepts.
Separate disease-agnostic measurement methods from SCN1A-specific biology.
Compare candidate endpoints against existing SCN2A natural-history studies.
Retain only endpoints validated as meaningful in SCN2A.
needs_validation: Whether each candidate endpoint is sensitive to change in SCN2A.
Whether age and developmental-stage distributions are comparable.
No therapeutic inference should be carried across the mechanistic mismatch.
